newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends slightly firmer, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends slightly firmer, more gains seen.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended slightly firmer on Tuesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised U.S. interest rates as expected. * Canada unit finished around C$1.3779 (US$0.7257) from Monday's close at C$1.3785 (US$0.7254). * Analysts said Fed rate move already priced into Canadian dollar, further strength seen.
"It was pretty much in line with what we expected. We took a back seat to what happened in the U.S.," one trader said.
The Canadian dollar hit a year low last week as financial markets factored in the Bank of Canada's stay-the-course reaction to a U.S. rate increase.

Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said last week that the central bank has more room to maneuver in reaction to U.S. interest rate hikes. But he cautioned that his comments should not be interpreted as a pledge not to raise rates.
With the Fed move out of the way, analysts said the unit may now benefit from Canada's brighter economic picture.
"The Fed move could allow the markets to focus on Canada's strong economic fundamentals," said Rob Palombi, senior fixed income analyst with MMS International.
He predicted the currency would trade between C$1.3690 (US$0.7304) and C$1.3730 (US$0.7283) in the near term.
In other economic news, the Quebec government unveiled a 1997/98 budget which forecast a deficit of C$2.2 billion in the year ended March 31, down from C$3.2 billion in fiscal 1996/97.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell to 1.2254 marks from 1.2277 marks on Monday and rose to 89.77 yen from Monday's 88.98 yen.
